cls: Biologic DMARD - tumor necrosis factor (TNF-alpha) blocker
pharm: Chimeric human-murine IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds soluble and transmembrane TNF-alpha, neutralizing its proinflammatory activity in immune-mediated inflammatory diseases.
quick: Rheumatoid arthritis: 3 mg/kg IV at weeks 0, 2, 6, then every 8 weeks (with methotrexate); 5 mg/kg for Crohn/UC/psoriasis
Intravenous infusion; not related to meals
Crosses placenta in 2nd/3rd trimester; delay infant live vaccines at least 6 months
Low/undetectable levels in milk; generally considered compatible
No specific dose adjustment; monitor for HBV reactivation/hepatotoxicity
No direct interaction; limit if on methotrexate (hepatotoxicity)
TB screening before/during, infections, hepatitis B, CBC, malignancy, infusion reactions
summary: Infliximab is a chimeric human-murine monoclonal antibody (TNF-alpha blocker) given by intravenous infusion for rheumatoid arthritis (with methotrexate), ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, plaque psoriasis, Crohn disease, and ulcerative colitis. Typical RA dosing is 3 mg/kg at weeks 0, 2, and 6, then every 8 weeks; most other indications use 5 mg/kg on the same induction schedule then every 6-8 weeks. It carries a BOXED WARNING for serious infections (including reactivation of latent tuberculosis, invasive fungal infections such as histoplasmosis, and bacterial sepsis) that may be fatal, and for malignancy including lymphoma and fatal hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma (especially in adolescents/young adults with Crohn/UC on thiopurines). Screen for latent TB and hepatitis B before initiation and monitor closely.
indications: Crohn disease (moderately to severely active) in adults and pediatric patients 6 years and older
Ulcerative colitis (moderately to severely active) in adults and pediatric patients 6 years and older
Rheumatoid arthritis (moderately to severely active) in combination with methotrexate
Chronic severe plaque psoriasis in adults

dosage.d: 3 mg/kg at weeks 0, 2, and 6, then every 8 weeks; may increase up to 10 mg/kg or dose as often as every 4 weeks for incomplete response
5 mg/kg at weeks 0, 2, and 6, then every 8 weeks; Crohn maintenance may increase to 10 mg/kg for loss of response
5 mg/kg at weeks 0, 2, and 6, then every 6 weeks
5 mg/kg at weeks 0, 2, and 6, then every 8 weeks

admin: Administer as an intravenous infusion over at least 2 hours using an in-line, sterile, low-protein-binding filter (1.2 micron or less)
Complete latent TB screening and hepatitis B testing before the first dose
Monitor for infusion reactions during and for a period after infusion; have resuscitation equipment available
Do not give live vaccines concurrently; bring vaccinations up to date before therapy
Reconstitute and dilute in 250 mL 0.9% sodium chloride; store reconstituted product per labeling and use promptly
moa: Infliximab is a chimeric IgG1-kappa monoclonal antibody (human constant, murine variable regions) that binds with high affinity to both soluble and transmembrane forms of human tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha), preventing it from binding its receptors. TNF-alpha is a key proinflammatory cytokine driving the inflammation, leukocyte infiltration, and tissue destruction of rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, and psoriasis. By neutralizing TNF-alpha, infliximab reduces inflammatory cell infiltration, downregulates adhesion molecules and acute-phase reactants, and can induce apoptosis of transmembrane-TNF-expressing cells.

absolute: Previous severe hypersensitivity reaction to infliximab products or any inactive ingredient (e.g., anaphylaxis)
Moderate to severe heart failure (NYHA III/IV) at doses greater than 5 mg/kg
relative: Active serious or chronic infection, active or latent tuberculosis
Mild heart failure (use lowest effective dose with monitoring)
Concurrent use of other biologic DMARDs or anakinra/abatacept (increased infection risk)
monitor: Active and latent tuberculosis before and during therapy
Signs of infection and sepsis; infusion reactions
Hepatitis B reactivation and liver enzymes
Complete blood count, malignancy, heart failure, and neurologic symptoms

preg: Infliximab actively crosses the placenta during the second and third trimesters and is detectable in infant serum for months after birth. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed. Live vaccines (e.g., BCG, rotavirus) should be delayed for at least 6 months in infants exposed in utero.
lact: Infliximab is present in human milk in low concentrations and is poorly absorbed by the infant; breastfeeding is generally considered compatible. Weigh benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment; infliximab is a monoclonal antibody not eliminated by the kidneys.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is provided for hepatic impairment. Monitor for hepatitis B reactivation and rare severe hepatic reactions, including autoimmune hepatitis and acute liver failure.

major: Other TNF blockers / biologic DMARDs (e.g., anakinra, abatacept) - increased serious infection risk; do not combine
Live vaccines - avoid during therapy (risk of vaccine-derived infection)
Tocilizumab and other biologics - increased immunosuppression
moderate: Immunosuppressants (methotrexate, azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, corticosteroids) - additive infection and (with thiopurines) hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma risk
Drugs metabolized by CYP450 with narrow index (warfarin, cyclosporine, theophylline) - TNF normalization may alter their levels
minor: No significant small-molecule pharmacokinetic interactions established
interactions.alcohol: No direct interaction; limit alcohol if on concomitant methotrexate due to hepatotoxicity risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Obtain tuberculin/IGRA testing and hepatitis B serologies before initiation; monitor CBC and liver enzymes during therapy.

common: Infusion-related reactions (fever, chills, urticaria, dyspnea, chest pain)
serious: Serious infections including tuberculosis (reactivation), invasive fungal (histoplasmosis, coccidioidomycosis), bacterial sepsis, opportunistic infections
Malignancies including lymphoma and fatal hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma (adolescents/young adults on thiopurines)
Hepatitis B reactivation and severe hepatic reactions
Demyelinating disease (multiple sclerosis, optic neuritis, Guillain-Barre)
Severe infusion reactions and serum-sickness-like delayed hypersensitivity

monitoring: Test for latent TB before therapy and monitor for active TB during and after treatment
Screen for hepatitis B before therapy; monitor carriers for reactivation
Observe for infusion reactions during and after each infusion
Signs and symptoms of infection at every visit; discontinue for serious infection/sepsis
CBC, liver enzymes, heart failure status, and new neurologic symptoms
counsel: This medicine lowers your immune defenses - call your doctor at the first sign of infection (fever, cough, night sweats, weight loss)
You will be tested for TB and hepatitis B before starting; report any history of TB or exposure to fungal infections
Tell the nurse immediately during the infusion if you feel itching, flushing, chest tightness, or trouble breathing
Do not receive live vaccines while on treatment; keep your vaccinations up to date beforehand
Report numbness/tingling, vision changes, unusual bleeding/bruising, persistent fever, or new lumps
pk: Clinical response often within 2 weeks; full effect over weeks (e.g., Crohn fistula response by week 2-6)
Maximum serum concentration at end of intravenous infusion
Therapeutic levels maintained with every 6-8 week dosing
Refrigerate vials at 2-8 C (36-46 F); do not freeze; protect from light; use reconstituted/diluted solution per labeling
pearls: BOXED WARNING: serious infections (reactivation of latent TB, invasive fungal infections, bacterial sepsis) that may be fatal - screen and treat latent TB before starting and monitor throughout
BOXED WARNING: malignancy, including lymphoma and fatal hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma (adolescents/young adults with Crohn/UC on azathioprine or 6-mercaptopurine)
RA dosing is unique: 3 mg/kg WITH methotrexate (reduces immunogenicity/antibody formation); other indications use 5 mg/kg
Doses above 5 mg/kg are contraindicated in moderate-to-severe (NYHA III/IV) heart failure
Infusion reactions are common - premedication and slow titration may be used; screen for hepatitis B before therapy
missed: Infliximab is administered in a clinical setting on a scheduled basis. If an infusion appointment is missed, contact the prescriber or infusion center to reschedule as soon as possible; the maintenance interval may need to be adjusted to maintain therapeutic levels.
overdose: Single doses up to 20 mg/kg have been administered without direct toxic effects. There is no known specific antidote. In case of overdose, monitor the patient closely for any adverse reactions or effects and institute appropriate symptomatic treatment immediately.
